To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the Bayesian machine paradigm is an effective way to model natural cognition and to build artificial systems that can learn to operate with uncertainty; (2) stochastic arithmetic is a plausible way to implement probabilistic inference in artificial systems; (3) the automatic design of electronic circuits for stochastic inference is a promising approach for the development of artificial cognition systems.

(1) the use of stochastic arithmetic allows to build a probabilistic circuit that computes soft inferences with few resources and (2) the use of Bayesian programs allows the automatic design of such circuits.

we have designed an automatic toolchain to build circuits computing Bayesian Program inference, and that the resulting circuits have a very low power consumption, which makes them very promising for embedded applications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of probabilistic circuits, i.e. electronic circuits that compute with probability distributions.
developing new models of computation, and with designing and testing new hardware architectures for them, in order to better understand the nature of natural cognition.
designing a machine that is capable of computing soft inferences in a way that is biologically plausible and can be implemented with a few resources.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were able to build a machine that computes the Bayesian filter in real time and that has been tested in real conditions.
our toolchain is capable of automatically designing and implementing an electronic circuit computing probabilistic inference from a high level description.
we have designed and implemented an automatic compiler from a high level description to a low level description, and that the low level description can be directly implemented and tested in hardware.
The main takeaway from our work is that
probabilistic programming can be used as a high level programming language to describe the behavior of non Von Neumann architectures.

we were able to design a circuit computing a Bayesian filter, with a complexity comparable to the one of a standard Von Neumann machine, and that can be efficiently implemented with few hardware resources.
the design of such a circuit is a non trivial task, which can be automatized using the toolchain we developed.
